flagged.evidence: The definition says a union of cells is a subcomplex when it contains “every cell in the closure” of each included cell. This does not require the closure itself to be contained. Start with the minimal CW structure on S^1 and attach a 2-cell by a map whose image is a proper closed subarc of the open 1-cell. The union consisting only of the open 2-cell contains no whole 1-cell in its closure, so it satisfies the written condition, but its closure contains the subarc omitted from the union. It is not a CW subcomplex.

Step 1.1 says X^n intersected with every closed cell is “either all of” that cell “or a union of boundary cells.” In the CW complex obtained by attaching a 2-cell to a proper subarc of the open 1-cell of the minimal S^1, X^1 intersected with the closed 2-cell is that proper subarc, not a union of cells. Thus the stated justification for applying the weak-topology clause is false.

The definition asserts that collapsing X^{n-1} minus e^{n-1}_β gives a quotient S^{n-1}, including n=1. For the standard one-vertex/one-edge CW structure on S^1, n=1 and X^0 minus e^0_β is empty, so X^0/emptyset is a one-point space, not S^0. Hence the stated map to S^0 and its induced endomorphism of reduced H_0(S^0;Z) are not defined. The final sentence about oriented reduced H_0 does not supply the missing map.

The displayed formula is asserted without excluding n=1, but its coefficient [e^n_α:e^{n-1}_β] is undefined in the one-vertex case by the preceding incidence-number definition. In particular, it cannot state a formula for d_1 as written; d_1 requires a separate endpoint calculation or an amended definition.

Step 1.1 gives the attaching incidence degree as 1+(-1)^{n-1}, while the Example states d_n=0 for odd n and d_n=2 for positive even n. At n=1 the displayed expression equals 2, and at n=2 it equals 0, exactly the reverse of the stated differential. Under the stated convention the needed expression is 1+(-1)^n.

The item calls constituent circles “1-cells.” But def-cell-attachment-by-a-characteristic-map defines an open 1-cell as the image of the interior of D^1, hence an open interval; a constituent circle is S^1 and includes the common vertex. Thus the proposed objects do not literally form the claimed cell structure. The intended conclusion remains correct when the punctured circles are the open cells and the circles are their closures.

Step 1.1 says H_n(X^n,A^n union X^{n-1};G) is the direct sum on cells outside A “by” thm-relative-homology-of-consecutive-cw-skeleta. That dependency states only the calculation of H_k(X^n,X^{n-1};G); it does not apply to the different pair with A^n adjoined. A quotient-CW-pair argument or an excision/relative-skeletal calculation is required and is not supplied.
